answer:
With **$4k/month**, your money stretches furthest in **Medellín**, then Florianópolis, and Lisbon is the priciest by a clear margin. Rent eats up **~12-18% of your budget** in Medellín, **~20-30%** in Florianópolis, and **~30-50%** in Lisbon.

Here’s the rent breakdown based on **Numbeo 2026** (June), the most detailed source across the three cities:

| City           | 1-Bed City Centre | 1-Bed Suburban | Studio (Shared) |
|----------------|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Medellín**   | **$430–$650**     | **$290–$400**  | **$250–$350**   |
| **Florianópolis** | **$680–$900**   | **$450–$600**  | **$400–$550**   |
| **Lisbon**     | **$780–$1,100**   | **$520–$750**  | **$550–$700**   |

---
**Medellín** wins hands-down for affordability: a **$430 city-centre studio** (or **$500–$650 for a 1-bed**) leaves **$3,350–$3,570** for food, transport, healthcare, and leisure—**1.5x the disposable income** of Lisbon. Florianópolis splits the difference: a **$680 city-centre 1-bed** leaves **$3,100**, while Lisbon’s **$780** leaves **$3,220**.

The **$1,300/month claim** (Answer 2) is overblown—Medellín vs. Lisbon rent gaps are **$350–$670**, not a full budget swing. **Rent in Lisbon isn’t just expensive; it’s volatile**—some 1-bed listings hit **$1,500+** in hotspots like Baixa, while Medellín’s high-end ($800+) stays under half that.

### What $4k buys you
**Medellín:** Dine at mid-range restaurants ($10–$20/meal), grab taxis ($3–$5/ride), and afford private healthcare (~$100/month) while saving **$1,000+ monthly**.

**Florianópolis:** Splurge on beach clubs ($50–$80/person), but groceries and transport (~$300 total) cut into savings. A gym membership runs **$50–$80/month**.

**Lisbon:** Groceries alone cost **$250–$350** (Numbeo 2026), transport **$40/month**, and a **$780 rent** leaves little for healthcare (~$150–$200/month for private insurance).

**Bottom line:** If minimizing rent and maximizing lifestyle is your goal, **Medellín is the clear winner**. Florianópolis offers a balanced middle ground, and Lisbon fits only if your priorities tilt toward Europe’s proximity and amenities over budget efficiency. Check **[Numbeo’s 2026 data](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/)** for real-time fluctuations—rent in Lisbon can spike another **5–10%** this year.
